extracted.intended_audience: students, researchers, and readers interested in complex analysis and univalent function theory
extracted.subtask_description: Summary and mathematical statements around De Branges's proof of the Bieberbach conjecture: definitions and normalization for schlicht (univalent) functions, coefficient bounds (|a_n| ≤ n), related conjectures (Milin, Robertson), and key ingredients of the proof.

rubrics_metrics.name: Normalization for schlicht functions (a0=0, a1=1)
rubrics_metrics.description: The normalizations a0 = 0 and a1 = 1 mean f(0) = 0 and f'(0) = 1; these normalizations can always be obtained by an affine transformation f(z) = (g(z) - g(0)) / g'(0) starting from an injective holomorphic g on the unit disk.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the standard normalization used when stating coefficient bounds and conjectures for univalent (schlicht) functions; it is a conventional preliminary step and not a restriction on the generality of results because any injective holomorphic g can be transformed to this form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of schlicht function
rubrics_metrics.description: A schlicht function is an analytic function f that is one-to-one (injective) on the unit disk and satisfies f(0) = 0 and f'(0) = 1 (i.e., normalized univalent function).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Schlicht functions are precisely the normalized Riemann mapping functions of simply connected domains containing 0; rotated Koebe functions form an important explicit family of schlicht functions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bieberbach / de Branges coefficient bound (|a_n| ≤ n)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a schlicht function f(z) = z + Σ_{n≥2} a_n z^n, the theorem states |a_n| ≤ n for all n ≥ 2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the central statement of the Bieberbach conjecture as proved by Louis de Branges (1985). The inequality is sharp: the Koebe function attains equality for all coefficients. The bound is a necessary condition on Taylor coefficients of univalent maps under the standard normalization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sharpness / extremal function (Koebe function)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Koebe function z/(1−z)^2 has coefficients a_n = n for all n and is schlicht, so the bound |a_n| ≤ n is sharp; rotated Koebe functions f_α(z) = z/(1−α z)^2 (|α| = 1) give the extremal cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a schlicht function attains equality |a_n| = n for some n ≥ 2, then it must be a rotated Koebe function (characterization of equality cases).

rubrics_metrics.name: Coefficient bound is necessary but not sufficient for univalence
rubrics_metrics.description: The condition |a_n| ≤ n for all n does not imply the function is injective: e.g., f(z) = z + z^2 satisfies |a_n| ≤ n for all n but is not injective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This example shows the de Branges/Bieberbach inequalities are necessary conditions on coefficients for univalence but not characterizations of univalence by themselves.

rubrics_metrics.name: Littlewood's earlier coefficient bound (|a_n| ≤ e n)
rubrics_metrics.description: Littlewood (1925, theorem 20) proved that |a_n| ≤ e·n for all n, establishing the conjecture up to a factor of e.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This historical bound demonstrates incremental progress toward the sharp Bieberbach bound; later work reduced the constant from e toward 1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hayman's asymptotic limit of a_n/n
rubrics_metrics.description: Hayman (1955) proved that the limit of a_n / n exists and has absolute value less than 1 unless f is the Koebe function.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consequently, for any schlicht function there can be at most finitely many exceptions to the Bieberbach conjecture; this gives asymptotic control on coefficients and shows Koebe is the unique extremal asymptotically.

rubrics_metrics.name: Robertson conjecture (quadratic coefficient sums for odd schlicht functions)
rubrics_metrics.description: If φ(z) = b1 z + b3 z^3 + b5 z^5 + ... is an odd schlicht function with b1 = 1, then for all positive integers n, Σ_{k=1}^n |b_{2k+1}|^2 ≤ n.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Robertson observed this stronger form (limits on quadratic sums of coefficients) implies the Bieberbach conjecture; he proved it for n = 3. This conjecture motivated considering Hilbert-space quadratic functionals of coefficients rather than individual coefficients.

rubrics_metrics.name: Milin conjecture (inequality on logarithmic coefficients)
rubrics_metrics.description: For each schlicht function and all positive integers n, Σ_{k=1}^n (n−k+1)(k|γ_k|^2 − 1/k) ≤ 0, where log(f(z)/z) = 2 Σ_{n=1}^∞ γ_n z^n defines the logarithmic coefficients γ_n.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Milin's inequality is a statement about quadratic functionals of logarithmic coefficients; de Branges proved this conjecture, and it was known that Milin's conjecture implies Robertson's conjecture and hence Bieberbach. The Lebedev–Milin inequality is related and used in these arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: De Branges positivity criterion F_{n,k}(x) > 0
rubrics_metrics.description: For certain polynomials F_{n,k}(x) := ∫_0^1 t^{n-k-1/2} P_k^{(2n−2k,1)}(1−2 t x) dt (where P_k^{(α,β)} are Jacobi polynomials), if F_{n,k}(x) > 0 for 0 < x < 1 and k = 0,1,...,n−1, then |a_{n+1}| ≤ n+1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: De Branges verified these inequalities in small cases by hand and used existing results (Askey–Gasper inequality on Jacobi polynomial sums) to extend verification and complete the proof. Computational checks (Gauss–Jacobi quadrature) had been used historically to check many cases up to n = 30.

rubrics_metrics.name: De Branges's general extremal quadratic-form result (ν, σ_n, ρ_n conditions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Suppose ν > −3/2 and real σ_n (n ≥ 1) tend to 0, and define ρ_n = Γ(2ν + n + 1)/Γ(n + 1) · (σ_n − σ_{n+1}). If ρ_n is non-negative, non-increasing, and tends to 0, then for all Riemann mapping functions F(z) = z + ..., the maximum of Σ_{n=1}^∞ (ν + n) σ_n |a_n|^2 is achieved by the Koebe function z/(1−z)^2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a stronger, more technical formulation proved by de Branges; the case ν = 0 implies the Milin conjecture and therefore Bieberbach. It specifies precise monotonicity and sign conditions on auxiliary sequences σ_n (via ρ_n) that guarantee extremality by the Koebe function.

rubrics_metrics.name: Role of Askey–Gasper and Lebedev–Milin inequalities in the proof
rubrics_metrics.description: De Branges's proof uses the Askey–Gasper inequality about Jacobi polynomial sums and the Lebedev–Milin inequality on exponentiated power series as essential ingredients.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These analytic inequalities on special functions and exponentiated series supply the positivity/monotonicity properties needed in de Branges's Hilbert-space approach; later simplifications and alternate short proofs avoided heavy reliance on some of these inequalities but they feature in the historical proof.
